lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Add a concise professional headline or summary.
items.because: The reader currently has to infer the target role from the experience and skills.

items.says: Make the portfolio link a direct, working URL to relevant work.
items.because: A repository or project page is more useful than a broad profile.

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is irrelevant to engineering qualifications and can introduce unnecessary bias.

items.says: Remove nationality unless it is specifically requested.
items.because: Nationality is not the same as work authorization and can create avoidable screening concerns.

items.says: Clarify the status of the expected graduation date.
items.because: It should remain current and not imply the degree is already completed.

items.says: Make the institution location identifiable and consider whether it needs to be listed.
items.because: Generic location labels may be unclear, while an unhelpful location takes space.

items.says: Make the institution location identifiable and consider whether it needs to be listed.
items.because: Generic location labels may be unclear, while an unhelpful location takes space.

items.says: Specify whether the 35% accuracy gain is relative or in percentage points.
items.because: The reader cannot assess the result's size without that distinction.

items.says: Define diagnostic accuracy and identify its evaluation set or baseline.
items.because: The reader cannot assess the result's reliability without those details.

items.says: Explain how reviewer disagreement was measured and over what sample.
items.because: The figures need measurement context.

items.says: Show that lower disagreement meant better review outcomes.
items.because: Greater agreement might instead suppress valid differences.

items.says: Clarify how equal accuracy against the SFT baseline was established.
items.because: The accuracy comparison needs supporting context.

items.says: Say whether the latency reduction is relative or absolute.
items.because: The size of the change is otherwise unclear.

items.says: Give the scope of the evaluation, if space allows.
items.because: Readers need it to judge how robust the result is.

items.says: Clarify whether the regressions were found before deployment and how the harness affected release decisions.
items.because: That would make its impact more concrete than saying it caught regressions.

items.says: This repeats the adapter fine-tuning and assistant-only loss masking in the first internship bullet.
items.because: The repeated method takes two bullets to describe.

items.says: Distinguish assistant-generated outputs from tool outputs and clarify which tokens received training loss.
items.because: The stated learning objective may confuse a technical reader.

items.says: Consider moving the diagnostics triage outcome earlier in the experience section.
items.because: It is one of the most compelling outcomes.

items.says: Clarify the backlog baseline and measurement period.
items.because: The reduction needs context to evaluate its impact.

items.says: Explain what the 800+ signals figure represents.
items.because: The scope of the screening is unclear.

items.says: The same backlog achievement appears again under the research-agent project.
items.because: The repetition raises questions about whether the work is distinct and correctly attributed.

items.says: Specify the GPU-memory measurement and workload behind the 4× reduction.
items.because: GPU memory can refer to several measures.

items.says: Clarify the workload or test conditions behind the p95 latency figures.
items.because: The figures need context.

items.says: Make clear that 200 ms is an automated regression threshold, not the achieved latency.
items.because: The threshold and measured result serve different purposes.

items.says: Correct the switch from past tense to present tense in “adds.”
items.because: The bullet describes past work.

items.says: Define the three-day release cycle and its comparison baseline.
items.because: Readers need to know what the figure measures and what it improved on.

items.says: Distinguish your contribution from the team's overall release process.
items.because: The bullet does not make that distinction clear.

items.says: Quantify the eliminated backlog or dispatch delay if a defensible measure is available.
items.because: The outcome is less quantified than the other bullets.

items.says: Ensure the outcome describes the migration's demonstrated effect.
items.because: It should not imply more than you can demonstrate.

items.says: Replace or remove the broad AI-first practices bullet.
items.because: It claims adoption, faster delivery and better outcomes without a specific system change or measurable result.

items.says: Explain the starting point and meaning of the 100× raw-conversation comparison.
items.because: It is unclear what grew 100×.

items.says: Explain how the under-10K-token working-context limit was measured.
items.because: The current phrasing leaves the result uncertain.

items.says: Add scope or test conditions for the 50-way fan-out, if available.
items.because: That would give the result more context.

items.says: Clarify how the elimination of deadlocks and lost results was verified.
items.because: “Removing” them is a strong claim that needs supporting evidence.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the metrics work as a contributor.
items.because: Implementing metrics and integrating existing implementations represent different contributions.

items.says: State what the 0.89 Kendall correlation was calculated against.
items.because: The validation result is hard to judge without an explicit comparison.

items.says: Explain what the 400+ report-level trials consisted of.
items.because: The scope of the validation is otherwise hard to judge.

items.says: This repeats the internship's triage backlog achievement under an unrelated research-agent project.
items.because: Its attribution is unclear unless the work is separate and distinguished.

items.says: Broaden the unusually short skills section with substantiated skills already evidenced elsewhere.
items.because: It is much narrower than the experience and projects suggest.

items.says: Check for missing tools and methods actually used in the described work.
items.because: The bullets describe CI, API work, caching, batching, event queues, BF16 and GRPO, but not all are represented in the skills list.

items.says: Make the “ML & Agents” category easier to scan.
items.because: It combines frameworks, methods and a broad capability.
